extracted.intended_audience: BBC journalists, programme-makers and online content producers (BBC staff and contributors creating TV, radio and online content)
extracted.subtask_description: Official BBC Editorial Guidelines covering values, standards and topic-specific guidance for producing and publishing BBC TV, radio and online content.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Editorial Guidelines (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editorial Guidelines are the BBC's values and standards. They apply to all our content, wherever and however it is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial Policy Guidance Notes supplement the Editorial Guidelines, with further explanation of their themes and practical tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Values
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles that underpin BBC content (listed under Section 1: The BBC's Editorial Values).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes links to the BBC Charter and Agreement and foundational values that should guide all output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and principles for ensuring accuracy in BBC content (Section 3: Accuracy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes 'Finding contributors' and 'Principles' related to sourcing and verification; also notes Mandatory Referrals for accuracy issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness, Contributors and Consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on fairness to contributors and obtaining consent (Section 6: Fairness, Contributors and Consent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers contributors, access agreements and editorial independence in dealing with contributors and sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles governing respect for privacy in reporting (Section 7: Privacy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes 'Principles' and 'Mandatory Referrals' relating to privacy, plus specific guidance such as Secret Recording and Anonymity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secret Recording
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on the use and ethical/legal considerations of secret recording (listed under Section 7 and Guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is revised guidance on Investigations and on Secret Recording; connects to privacy and mandatory referrals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance specific to investigative journalism, including revised Investigations Guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes practical guidance and interplay with secrecy, privacy and mandatory referrals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance related to granting or protecting anonymity for contributors and sources (From > Section 6: Fairness, Contributors and Consent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linked under privacy and contributor-related principles; includes mandatory referral triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harm and Offence (including Imitative Behaviour)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for assessing potential harm or offence caused by content (Section 5: Harm and Offence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes specific topics such as Imitative Behaviour and substances (Alcohol, Smoking, Solvent Abuse and Illegal Drugs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Children and Young People as Contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Special protections and rules when children/young people contribute to BBC content (Section 9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains Mandatory Referrals and principles about consent, safeguarding and editorial handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Integrity and Independence from External Interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules to preserve editorial integrity and independence from external interests (Section 14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes BBC Worldwide Advertising and Sponsorship Guidelines and guidance on external relationships and funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: External Relationships and Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards governing relationships with external organisations and funding arrangements (Section 16 / 14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies mandatory referrals and practices to avoid conflicts of interest and preserve editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-Use and Reversioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and procedures for re-using and re-versioning BBC material (Section 13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes 'Principles', 'Introduction', and 'Mandatory Referrals' relating to re-use and reversioning rights and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interacting with our Audiences (Interactivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on audience interaction formats including phone-ins, user-generated content, mobile content, games and interactive TV (Section 17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers technical advice, prizes, voting, competitions, awards, telephone services, pre-recorded/repeated programmes, and the Interactivity Technical Advice and Contracts Unit (ITACU).

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitions, Votes and Awards (including Code of Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and code of conduct for running competitions, votes and awards (Appendix 2: Code of Conduct for Competitions and Voting; Section 17 items).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes mandatory referrals, procedures for prizes, voting mechanics, transparency and fairness requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Game Shows, Quizzes and Talent Shows
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific rules for game shows, quizzes and talent programmes (Section 17: Game Shows; Talent Shows and Programmes Offering Life-Changing Opportunities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses fairness, participant treatment, prize handling and editorial obligations for life-changing opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phone-in Programmes and User Generated Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for phone-ins and handling user-generated content online (listed under Section 17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes moderation, verification, consent and technical/contractual advice (ITACU).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-recorded or Repeated Programmes
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for handling pre-recorded or repeated broadcasts (Section 17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers editorial checks, corrections, and handling of material when not live.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prizes, Voting and Awards Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational rules for administering prizes, voting and awards (Section 17 related links).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes fairness, transparency and contractual/technical requirements; links to code of conduct and ITACU.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Interactivity Technical Advice and Contracts Unit (ITACU)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to specialist unit providing technical and contractual advice for interactive services (Section 17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ITACU provides guidance and contracts support for interactivity, competitions and services involving audience participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and Responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on roles and responsibilities for implementing and following the Editorial Guidelines (From > Section 2: Using the Guidelines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies who in the organisation is responsible for decisions, mandatory referrals and compliance with the Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using the Guidelines / Principles and Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical advice on how to use the Editorial Guidelines and the underlying principles and practices (Section 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes Editorial Justification and links to other sources of advice; explains how guidance notes supplement the Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to record and justify editorial decisions where appropriate (listed under Section 2: Using the Guidelines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to document why editorial choices that might be contentious or risky were made, linking to accountability processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Referrals
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific topics and situations that must be referred to editorial policy/legal/other specialists (appears across many sections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pages repeatedly flag 'Mandatory Referrals' for issues such as accuracy, privacy, children, re-use, and external relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and standards for accountability, feedback and complaints (Section 19: Accountability; Feedback and Complaints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links to BBC Complaints processes, the BBC Trust and Ofcom Broadcasting Code; includes how to handle adjudications and public interest considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Protection Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to legal obligations under the Data Protection Act relevant to handling personal data (listed under Related Links / Section 18: The Law).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connects legal compliance to privacy guidance and mandatory referral processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising and the BBC Brand
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on advertising, sponsorship and the use of the BBC brand (From > Section 14: Editorial Integrity and Independence from External Interests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes BBC Worldwide Advertising and Sponsorship Guidelines and rules to separate editorial from commercial interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigations and Secret Recording: Revised Guidance (news)
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcement of revised guidance on Investigations and Secret Recording (Latest News items).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals updates to existing guidance and that staff should consult the revised notes for practice changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong Language on Radio
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance and Ofcom advice on the use of strong language on radio programmes (Latest News item).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alerts programme-makers to regulator guidance and appropriate editorial controls for broadcast language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and Editorial Guidance Modules
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of BBC Academy training modules covering topics such as Accuracy, Impartiality, Strong Language, Violence, Secret Recording, Consent, Children, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages staff to use training modules to understand and apply the Guidelines in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related External Standards and Links
rubrics_metrics.description: References to external regulatory and advisory bodies and documents (Ofcom Broadcasting Code, Defence Advisory Notice Committee, BBC Trust).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides staff to consult external codes and adjudications alongside BBC internal guidance when making editorial decisions.
